content.text:
The following report from the customer app indicates that it seems to be possible to not have bus IOs written out correctly at the end of action lists. 

<pasted_content id="99a0">
2. The ir380r01 / e71 wait (13:25:13 → 13:32:49)

The UP4 retreat (up4.py, P8–P12) puts its a123 writes inside the motion's action list. NOVA's motion service fires them as the robot passes the points:
- location 3 (P10): a123=True
- location 5 (end, P12): a123=False, a60=True, a23=False

Comparing the motion service log with the bus-I/O service log:

┌────────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┬───────────────────────────┐
│        Run         │ Location 3 write │ Location 5 write │     Motion "finished"     │
├────────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ 13:23:01 (good)    │ 13:23:03.022     │ 13:23:05.001     │ 13:23:05.134              │
├────────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ 13:24:52 (failing) │ 13:24:54.164     │ missing          │ 13:24:56.277, reported OK │
├────────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ 13:33:17 (good)    │ 13:33:18.864     │ 13:33:20.844     │ —                         │
└────────────────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘

- In the failing run a123=True was written but the location-5 batch never was. The writes after it at .285/.286 each have their own HTTP PUT, so they are the Folge's next steps, not the lost batch.
- The Folge still logged UP4: P12 erreicht, Profilfrei 21 gesetzt although a60 was never written. The motion service reported success, so the log line is misleading.
- a123 therefore stayed TRUE from 13:24:54 until your manual write. That write is the only browser PUT in the whole log: 13:32:23 from the Settings bus-signals page. e71 came 26 s later.
- It was not a lost bus message. During the wait the backup re-poll ran alongside the normal wait and kept reading e71 low, so the cell PLC really held it.
- The whole cell then stalled behind ir380r01: ir340r01, ir340r02, ir350r01 and ir370r01 waited 417–459 s on their entry releases. They were symptoms, not causes.
- The NATS reconnect falls inside the wait but did not cause it or end it.
</pasted_content id="99a0">

 Pleas check under which circumstance this might happen
I'll trace how the SDK turns in-list `io_write` actions into motion-service triggers and how execution ends, to find the paths where the final location's writes can be skipped.

name: path-triggers-port
description: "Path triggers (io_write at=) ported from NDX-155 to main as PR #509 on 2026-09-03; distance_offset API never landed; verification numbers"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  modified: 2026-09-17T13:09:20.704Z
---

Path triggers ("Bahnschaltpunkte") were ported from `feat/NDX-155-simple-custom-actions` to branch `feat/path-triggers` → PR #509 (2026-09-03). Design: reuse the command-routine API's `AtTrigger` models; builders `at_path_fraction/at_distance/at_time` come from `nova.command_routines.commands`, sugar `after_*/before_*` in `nova/actions/path_trigger.py`; resolution in `MotionGroup._resolve_set_outputs` → `MovementControllerContext.set_outputs`.

**Why:** `SetIO.distance_offset` (assumed by `feat/path-triggers-distance-offset`) never reached service-manager master; the 26.7.0 instance at 172.31.10.234 silently ignores the field (probe: fired at location 1.011 instead of ~1.33). Client-side FK resolution stays.

**Naming decision 2026-09-17 (Dirk, finalizing #509 that day):** the `after_time/before_time/after_distance/before_distance` sugar is replaced by two builders `after_start(seconds=|millimeters=)` / `before_target(seconds=|millimeters=)`. Reason: `before_*` read as "before the next motion *starts*" (wrong segment); units were invisible at the call site; robot programmers know start-point/target-point vocabulary (KUKA `TRIGGER WHEN PATH=-50`, ABB `TriggIO Distance \Start`). `at_path_fraction/at_distance/at_time` stay untouched — released in v5.11.0 via `nova.command_routines` (#488) and mirror the API wire types; only drop `at_time/at_distance` from `nova.actions` exports. Unit-library research (2026-09-17): no mainstream lib gives static dimension typing; pint 0.26 needs py>=3.12 and costs ~300 ms import. Dirk decided: `seconds` accepts `float | timedelta`, `millimeters` accepts `float`; pint/duck-typed quantities deferred ("we can evaluate and add pint later"). Keep this in mind if a customer asks for unit values — the design is: accept any object with `.m_as(unit)`, never construct quantities ourselves, no dependency. Rename landed as commit 40597ec4 on #509 (2026-09-17), rebased onto Dirk's main merge aa161e6e; PR body rewritten; example verified live on 172.31.10.67 (the current instance, per Dirk's main-worktree `.env`). #509 squash-merged to main as 51861139 on 2026-09-17; worktree and local branch removed. `feat/path-triggers-distance-offset` (local only, unported server-side-offset experiment) was deliberately left in place. Fresh worktrees need `uv sync --all-extras` for the full unit suite.

**How to apply:** If the API later ships a distance offset, the change is local to `path_trigger_resolver.py` and `to_set_io`. Live check pattern that worked: stream `stream_execute` while polling `controller_ios_api.list_io_values` for `OUT#1`; resolved vs observed toggles matched within ~0.01 location. The rest of NDX-155 (async actions) still lives on PR #405. Teaching `datasets` endpoints returned HTTP 500 on both virtual instances that day. Related: [[state-stream-stall-fix]].

name: ci-intermediate-stop-regression
description: "Since 2026-09-18 integration CI failed test_forward_to_intermediate_target_keeps_the_session_open on every branch — new NOVA build publishes execute state level-based; cursor completed a resume on the previous stop's re-published END frames. Fixed in worktree fix/intermediate-stop-resume."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 78bb3f32-cd75-4fb5-bc5f-796b30b090ab
  modified: 2026-09-18T15:19:57.544Z
---

`tests/nova/cell/test_trajectory_executor_integration.py::test_forward_to_intermediate_target_keeps_the_session_open`
failed deterministically on every branch from 2026-09-18 ~08:00 UTC: after `forward_to(1.0)` the resume
`forward()` resolved at ~1.0–1.07 instead of 2.0 while the robot ran on to the end.

**Why:** Not any PR's code: run 35322738024 (chore/extract-sbom-information, same main commit 51861139
and same `wandelbots-api-client==26.7.0.dev24` as the last green run 35222878394 on 2026-09-17) failed
identically. Only variable: the fresh NOVA instance from `scripts/create_nova_instance.py` (portal
sandbox, latest server build). Reproduced on Dirk's instance 172.31.13.138: the new build publishes
execute state level-based (wbr!2262) — after the stop at 1.0 it re-publishes `TrajectoryEnded@1.0`
every step until it takes up the next start (then WAIT_FOR_IO → RUNNING → END@2.0). The cursor's
`ended` completion had no stale guard (only `paused` had `may_complete_as_paused`), so the resumed
operation completed on the old END frames (final_location 1.0).

**How to apply:** Do not blame PRs for this failure (PR #520 was wrongly suspected at first). Fix:
`TrajectoryExecutionMachine.on_start` records the terminal state a `start` leaves (kind + location) and
`process_motion_state` ignores frames repeating it until a different frame arrives. A start issued at
the very end yields WAIT_FOR_IO then END again, so the filter lifts there too — do not replace this with a
"seen RUNNING" guard, it would hang that case. Probe pattern that found it: tap `stream_state()` per
group, log (state kind, location, standstill) changes around the resume. Local repro needs the main
repo's `.env` copied into the worktree with NOVA_API swapped.

name: state-machine-armed-fix
description: "2026-09-17 fix: TrajectoryExecutionMachine armed/transient/rest redesign after the robot_only_loop hang (stale PausedByUser + standstill jitter); decisions vs ADR 002 / feat/pause-on-io-resume; branch + follow-up rebase"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9474d208-f06e-4b3e-a691-e4760dbac378
  modified: 2026-09-22T09:52:12.163Z
---

Fix branch `fix/trajectory-state-machine-armed-transient-rest` → **PR #516** (opened
2026-09-17, off main, cherry-picks the per-frame debug log b7939d1c from
`lab/state-machine-frame-debug`). Live verification on `kuka-clone` still open. Plan:
`~/.claude/plans/the-problem-is-that-majestic-noodle.md`. Frame trace artifact:
https://claude.ai/artifact/MVGXsf84PxHjFGV3Tzo58x (log `/tmp/exec.log`, 2026-09-16 16:21).

**Controller contract (Dirk):** at the start of an execution the stream shows
`standstill=True` + `TrajectoryPausedByUser` (parked, level-based) until motion begins;
`standstill` may flip one cycle before the discriminator goes RUNNING, and `standstill` can
jitter True while RUNNING (upstream bug, to be fixed in RAE). After a resume the previous
terminal state (PAUSED_ON_IO / END) is re-published for a few cycles.

**Decisions 2026-09-17 (all my recommendations accepted):**
- New `armed` state (start → armed → executing on first RUNNING); parked frames are no-ops;
  `request_pause()` external signal from `cursor.pause()`; `start(stale_terminal=…)`.
- Transient states (`pausing`/`ending`) return to `executing` on RUNNING.
- Rest states: `paused(USER) ∧ Running` and `ended ∧ Running` → `error` +
  `UnexpectedTrajectoryState(ErrorDuringMovement)` raised from the cursor monitor;
  `paused(IO) ∧ Running` → executing (ADR 002 hedge kept). Record as ADR 003 amending ADR 002 §1.
- One-shot `execute()`: external USER pause after motion → raise; IO pause → op completes
  `paused_on_io`, `move_forward` warns + detaches (early return) until the supervisor lands.
- Absorb ADR 002 §1–2 machine/cursor parts from `feat/pause-on-io-resume` (PauseReason,
  PausedOnIO → paused, `OperationResult.paused_on_io`, port `test_trajectory_cursor_io_pause.py`);
  the `_stale_terminal_state` cursor guard and `_resume_observed` edge are superseded.

**2026-09-22 rebase onto main:** main had #521 (identity stale-terminal filter: a start out of
ended/paused ignores frames with the same kind+location until a different frame; a start at
the very end is answered WAIT_FOR_IO → END, so never use a "seen RUNNING" guard) and #512
(pause() always queues, never returns None). Dropped my cursor-side `arm(stale_terminal=…)` /
`_movement_has_room` in favour of #521's filter hosted in `armed` (set in `on_start`), with a
`pause_requested` exemption. Commit cba1c40b, force-pushed with lease.

**Scratch branch `lab/interlock-with-armed-machine`** (2026-09-22, pushed): merge of #516 into
`lab/interlock-with-pause` (= feat/pause-on-io-resume + zone-interlock, rebased on main 6.0.0)
for live interlock tests before #516 lands. Dirk's requirement: `forward()` from an ended
trajectory (no-op) must be safe regardless of WAIT_FOR_IO → kept the branch's
`accept_repeated_terminal()` as `arm(accept_repeated_terminal=…)` with a conservative
`_movement_has_room` (unknown trajectory → has room). Throwaway once #516 merges: then rebase
`lab/interlock-with-pause` onto main and port that hint into #516's line if still wanted.

**Why:** hang in `execute()` on main today; #509 (triggers) open 2 weeks blocks the stacked
resume branch; redesign the machine once.

**How to apply / follow-up:** after this fix merges, rebase `feat/pause-on-io-resume`
(stacked on `feat/path-triggers`): drop its machine commit parts + `_stale_terminal_state`,
keep io_condition/supervisor/NATS. Related: [[pause-on-signal]], [[path-triggers-port]].
